claims.text: The company operates general-merchandise discount stores and a companion e-commerce/digital-fulfillment business across the United States, selling apparel, home goods, food, beauty and hardline products, with revenue earned through in-store and digital/same-day retail sales.

Full-year FY2020 comparable sales grew 19.3% (7.2 points from stores, 145% digital comparable-sales growth), with Q4 comparable sales up 20.5%, and total revenue rose to $93.6 billion from $78.1 billion.
Target stated it is not providing sales and EPS guidance for fiscal 2021 and beyond, citing continued uncertainty.

Full-year operating margin rose to 7.0% from 6.0% and after-tax return on invested capital rose to 23.5% from 16.0%, while capital expenditures fell to $2.649 billion from $3.027 billion and cash rose to $8.511 billion from $2.577 billion.
Target paid no share repurchases in Q4 2020 but said it resumed share repurchases in fiscal 2021, with approximately $4.5 billion of remaining board-authorized capacity.
Management said the decision to withhold FY2021 guidance reflected continued COVID-19-related uncertainty.
Same-day fulfillment services grew 212% in Q4 (Drive Up up more than 500%), and the company said higher digital fulfillment and supply-chain costs affected gross margin.
FY2020 added more than $15 billion of sales -- more than the company's combined sales growth over the prior 11 years -- alongside operating-margin expansion to 7.0% and ROIC of 23.5%.
The company said it gained approximately $9 billion in market share and continued to gain share across all five of its core merchandising categories, without disclosing category-level figures.

Cash rose to $8.511 billion and capital expenditure fell to $2.649 billion from $3.027 billion even as operating cash flow rose to $10.525 billion from $7.117 billion, and the company resumed share repurchases (up to ~$4.5 billion) in fiscal 2021.
Management explicitly declined to give FY2021 sales or EPS guidance due to continued uncertainty, leaving no company-provided forward anchor.

Digital comparable sales accounted for roughly two-thirds of Q4 comparable-sales growth, up 118% in the quarter and 145% for the full year; this release does not address whether that pace continues or normalizes.
The current portion of long-term debt rose more than sevenfold to $1.144 billion as of January 30, 2021, from $161 million a year earlier, a maturity step-up not explained in this release.

The company said higher digital fulfillment and supply-chain costs already affected gross margin even amid record sales growth, a cost structure that continued digital-penetration growth could keep embedding.
